cells.tense: You're here, and you're letting fall what was actually ready to fall.
cells.verb: clearing out what couldn't hold once you saw it plainly
cells.place: in the underneath of things, where you can see how they really work
cells.ask: Take the clear seeing and give it a small, daily shape — one quiet piece of work you return to, kept going by attention rather than by the next big moment of clearing — so the sight stays yours after the rubble is gone.
cells.core:
You're here, and you're letting fall what was actually ready to fall. You can see how a thing works underneath the way it presents itself, and when the underneath doesn't hold the surface up, you don't prop it — you let it go, and it turns out that was the honest move. Nothing is being torn down for the feeling of it; what goes was already false.

There's an invitation in that, if you want it. The seeing came fast; what it's free to feed now is something slow. One small practice, returned to on ordinary days, kept lit by attention rather than by flash. Clearing shows you the ground. Steady work is how you come to live on it.
cells.sheetLine: What falls when you look at it was already false. You can build on that.

cells.tense: You're already in the moment after everything comes down, and you keep arriving there early.
cells.verb: knocking out whatever shows a crack
cells.place: in the underneath of things, where every surface shows its workings
cells.ask: Before you take the next thing down, carry it to someone who holds the same understanding — say what you see and hear what they've kept and why — and let one shared piece stand unaltered long enough to find out whether it was false or just older than you.
cells.core:
You're already in the moment after everything comes down, and you keep arriving there early. Seeing how things work underneath has become seeing where they'll fail, and once you see a flaw you can't leave the thing standing — so nothing gets to stand. The clearing has started running on its own and calling itself freedom.

Some of what you're pulling down was holding something. The medicine is on the other side of the room from where you're working: the meanings people share and keep passing along, not because they're unexamined but because they've carried weight. Bring what you see to someone who holds the same question. Let one inherited thing stay up while you learn it from the inside. When the clearing comes back to itself, what falls will be what needed to — and only that.
cells.sheetLine: You're tearing down everything with a crack. Some of it was load-bearing.

cells.tense: You're still standing under something that has already stopped holding.
cells.verb: holding up what has already quit holding you
cells.place: in the underneath of things, where you can already see that it doesn't work
cells.ask: Rather than forcing yourself to let go, start building the small, workable arrangement that fits what you actually know to be true — one piece that's clear and reliable — and let the old frame come down on its own as the new one takes the weight.
cells.core:
You're still standing under something that has already stopped holding. You can see how it works underneath — you can see that it doesn't — and you're keeping it up anyway, hands on the beam, because the moment it falls is a door you'd rather not have already walked through. But that door is behind you. What's left is the holding.

Pushing yourself to drop it is the wrong direction; the arms are tired enough. Put the effort somewhere else instead: into making one small arrangement that actually fits what you know is true. Clear, reliable, something that makes sense when you stand in it. As that takes weight, the old thing loses its last reason to stay up, and letting it fall becomes an ordinary act instead of a catastrophe. What falls then was already false.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up something that already fell. Build what fits what's true instead.

cells.tense: You're in a room where something is already coming down, and you haven't looked up yet.
cells.verb: letting things fall without knowing you're the one letting them
cells.place: in the underneath of things, where you've seen more than you've admitted
cells.ask: Move toward one thing you plainly want — not analyze it, move — and watch what holds and what doesn't on the way; the thing that's about to fall will show itself in whatever you walk straight through.
cells.core:
You're in a room where something is already coming down, and you haven't looked up yet. You've seen how it works underneath; you can feel that it doesn't hold; some part of you has already stopped leaning on it. But the falling is being described as something happening to you, or not described at all. The clearing is in motion. The one who started it is standing with the pen down.

The way back is earlier and simpler than the seeing. Pick one thing you genuinely want and move toward it — from the wanting, not from the analysis. Whatever you walk straight through on the way, you'll know was already false. Whatever you find yourself walking around was holding something. When the clearing is yours again, what falls will be what needed to, and you'll know you let it.
cells.sheetLine: Something's already coming down. You're the one letting it, and you haven't said so.
